explanation: Together they filter about 180 litres of fluid from the blood each day, then take almost all of it back, leaving only about 1 to 2 litres as urine.

claims.text: The kidneys filter the blood and produce urine.
The lungs, adrenal glands and tonsils do not make urine.
The kidneys filter about 180 litres of fluid from the blood each day.
The kidneys reabsorb almost all of the filtered fluid, leaving only about 1 to 2 litres of urine a day.

evidence.restatement: The kidneys filter blood and produce urine.
The lungs exchange gases, the adrenal glands make hormones and the tonsils fight infection; none makes urine.
A normal filtration rate of about 125 mL a minute adds up to about 180 litres of filtrate a day.
